humanities_role_explanation: LongFact spans 38 topics (humanities is only one of four supercategories, alongside STEM, social sciences and other); the items test general long-form factuality, not disciplinary humanities competence. Humanities topics (history, philosophy, music, movies, world religions) merely supply prompt content.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Text-only: fact-seeking text prompts elicit long-form text responses, which are decomposed into atomic facts and checked via Google Search.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Models answer open-ended fact-seeking prompts with long-form responses (multi-paragraph). Factuality is scored by decomposing responses into individual facts and rating each as supported, not supported, or irrelevant (SAFE), aggregated with F1@K. This is long-form factuality of generated text.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Scoped to a single capability (long-form factuality), though across 38 topics. It is not a broad multi-task benchmark.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: Thirteen models: Gemini-Ultra/Pro, GPT-4-Turbo/GPT-4/GPT-3.5-Turbo, Claude-3-Opus/Sonnet/Haiku, Claude-2.1/2.0/Instant, PaLM-2-L-IT-RLHF/PaLM-2-L-IT.

quantitative_metrics.note: F1@K (K=64 and K=178), precision, recall, counts of supported/not-supported/irrelevant facts; SAFE-human agreement (72%).

summary: The paper introduces LongFact, a GPT-4-generated prompt set of 2,280 fact-seeking questions across 38 topics, together with SAFE, an LLM-agent evaluator that checks atomic facts via Google Search, and F1@K, a metric combining precision with recall relative to a preferred response length. Thirteen LLMs are benchmarked, with larger models generally more factual.
key_findings: SAFE agrees with crowdsourced human annotations on 72.0% of 16,011 facts and wins 76% of 100 disagreement cases (humans 19%), at over 20x lower cost. GPT-4-Turbo is best (F1@64 95.0, F1@178 66.4). Larger models generally achieve better long-form factuality, and RLHF improves it.
facets_explanation: Prompts are generated by GPT-4 from manually selected topics, with manual deduplication. There is no fixed answer key: the reference is dynamic Google Search evidence, applied by an LLM agent (SAFE) that rates each atomic fact. Correctness requires external world knowledge, since the prompts name only entities or concepts. SAFE was validated against crowdsourced annotations from Min et al. (2023) and the authors' own researcher re-annotation.
results_explanation: Table 2: GPT-4-Turbo F1@64 95.0 and F1@178 66.4, the best of thirteen models on 250 random LongFact-Objects prompts. The headline metric is F1@K, which is not in the metric list, so it is recorded as other. The paper reports comparisons for LongFact-Concepts being easier than LongFact-Objects and for responses with versus without the postamble, but gives no single point gap, so reported_format_gap_points is null. The human comparison is SAFE agreement with crowdsourced annotators, not a human baseline on model performance.
